data.narrative:
Insitro, a Series C biotech company founded by Daphne Koller, has raised $1.1B+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 public comps (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private companies in Biotech & Health, including stage-matched peers Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), and New Limit ($3.1B).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier to the $1.1B raised proxy, yielding $1.9B. Peer-median analysis benchmarks against 3 same-sector, same-stage companies, which have a median valuation of $3.8B and a range of $3.1B–$10.3B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied because Insitro's revenue is not disclosed. 

Triangulating the two applicable methods produces a valuation range of $1.6B (low) to $4.4B (high), with a median of $2.8B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around (i) positioning relative to Colossal's outlier $10.3B valuation and (ii) the absence of revenue-based scaling metrics. Without visibility into Insitro's own financials and burn profile, the stage-progression floor and peer median provide reasonable bounds for the current Series C round.
